local_articles.snippet: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli has delivered one of the most sensational triumphs in the long history of the Italian Grand Prix by becoming the first home winner in 60 years after starting from 19th on the grid. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver, from nearby Emilia-Romagna, claimed his seventh win of the season on Sunday to extend his lead in the drivers’ title race as he seeks to become Italy’s first world champion since Ferrari’s Alberto Ascari in 1953. local_articles.title: F1 leader Kimi Antonelli wins Italian GP after epic charge from the back
local_articles.snippet: Kimi Antonelli took a big step to becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1 history with a fightback for the ages at his home grand prix on Sunday. Antonelli stormed to victory at the Italian Grand Prix, despite having started 19th on the grid. It took the Mercedes driver fewer than 17 laps to fight his way to the front. {{^htLoading}} {{/htLoading}} The rest of the race was spent tussling with teammate and title rival George Russell for the lead. Antonelli passed him for the final time with three laps remaining, going on to become the first Italian to win at Monza in 60 years. "Oh my God ... It feels like a dream," Antonelli said on team radio after crossing the line. Unbelievable, unbelievable'"I did not expect it," Antonelli said later. "Unbelievable, unbelievable. I am so happy, I could not have imagined to be here today but we managed to pull it off and I am really, really happy."

World No. 1 Hania El Hammamy remains favored (90.4% win rate in 2025/26, defending 2025 Qatar champion, with upside in London where World No. 2 Amina Orfi is defending champion). However, Orfi's overtake odds are materially higher than 0.23: she won the 2026 World Championships and British Open (beating El Hammamy), led the tour in % of points won (61.8% vs 59.6%), came within one match of #1 at June's Tour Finals, and PSA previews highlight Doha as her immediate shot at #1—especially with El Hammamy facing returning former #1 Nouran Gohar in the Qatar quarter-finals. Meanwhile, Gohar (returning at #6 seed after a 1-year absence, skipping London) has virtually no mathematical path to #1 by Sept 21, and Nour El Sherbini (skipping London, #3 seed in Qatar) has only a remote tail chance (0.015). Accordingly, we shift El Hammamy 0.72 -> 0.63, Orfi 0.23 -> 0.35, El Sherbini 0.03 -> 0.015, and drop Gohar.
